title: tetraclea coulteri var. subinclusa
intro: Tetraclea coulteri var. subinclusa, commonly known as Coulter's Toothwort or Coulter's Coralroot, is a plant species belonging to the Gentianaceae family. It is used in traditional medicine to treat various health issues, including digestive problems, and has been found to have anti-inflammatory properties, which may provide relief from pain and swelling. The therapeutic actions of Tetraclea coulteri var. subinclusa include its ability to stimulate digestion, reduce inflammation, and exhibit antimicrobial activity, making it a potential treatment for various conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include iridoid glycosides and other alkaloids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties, although further research is needed to fully understand its effects and potential applications.
